posts.title: Supplier DIFOT: Measure the Delivery That Actually Matters
posts.summary: Supplier DIFOT is only useful when it compares delivery performance against a clear, preserved commitment and an agreed delivery point. This article explains why original PO dates and quantities matter, when an accepted delay should not count as a miss, and how Incoterms can create very different views of the same delivery.
posts.author: Daniel Hampton

posts.title: Why Supply Chain Planning Needs a Stronger Professional Identity
posts.summary: Many people enter supply chain planning through operations, purchasing, warehousing or production rather than through a formal planning pathway. Practical experience is valuable, but planners also need a shared body of knowledge that helps them understand why planning decisions are made, not just how to complete the tasks in front of them.
posts.author: Daniel Hampton

posts.title: How Lot Size Affects Stock Turnover
posts.summary: Lot size is the quantity ordered or produced in one batch, and it has a direct effect on how long inventory stays in the business. Smaller lots can improve stock turnover, while larger lots may reduce ordering and handling effort but can leave more stock sitting in storage.
